message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-09-12 05:10 IST to 2026-09-13 05:10 IST (2026-09-11 23:40 UTC to 2026-09-12 23:40 UTC)

No newly reported vulnerability in the last 24 hours could be tied directly and confidently to a product edition in the combined, deduplicated primary inventory from `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt`. Two critical CVEs newly published during the window affect a WordPress plugin and require deployment confirmation.

### Possible matches needing review

**CVE-2026-78159 — The Events Calendar unauthenticated remote code execution**

- **Affected product/component:** StellarWP The Events Calendar WordPress plugin, versions through 6.17.3.
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 9.8 (CNA/Wordfence).
- **Description:** Insufficient validation of a widget classes map can allow an unauthenticated attacker to reach a callable-invocation path and execute server-side code when the required event-comment conditions are present.
- **Why it may be relevant:** WordPress is monitored, but The Events Calendar is not explicitly listed. Confirm whether this plugin is installed before treating the finding as applicable.
- **Source:** [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-78159); [Patchstack advisory](https://patchstack.com/database/wordpress/plugin/the-events-calendar/vulnerability/wordpress-the-events-calendar-plugin-6-17-3-unauthenticated-code-injection-to-remote-code-execution-vulnerability)

**CVE-2026-78006 — The Events Calendar unauthenticated deserialization to remote code execution**

- **Affected product/component:** StellarWP The Events Calendar WordPress plugin, versions through 6.17.4.
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 9.8 (CNA/Wordfence).
- **Description:** An unsafe widget-instance validation and deserialization path can allow unauthenticated server-side code execution when comments are enabled and visible on events.
- **Why it may be relevant:** WordPress is monitored, but The Events Calendar is not explicitly listed. Confirm whether this plugin is installed before treating the finding as applicable.
- **Source:** [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-78006); [Patchstack advisory](https://patchstack.com/database/wordpress/plugin/the-events-calendar/vulnerability/wordpress-the-events-calendar-plugin-6-17-4-unauthenticated-php-object-injection-to-remote-code-execution-vulnerability)

### MongoDB ecosystem sweep

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations and libraries, MongoDB-owned notices whose titles may omit “MongoDB,” GitHub advisories, CVE/NVD-oriented records, CISA sources, and credible government reporting.

No credible MongoDB ecosystem vulnerability was newly reported or materially updated within this exact 24-hour window. Vendor disclosures dated September 8 and a government notice dated September 10/11 without a verifiable in-window timestamp were excluded as stale or freshness-unverified.

### Closing

Immediate review is recommended only to determine whether The Events Calendar is deployed on any monitored WordPress site; if present, both critical findings apply to overlapping vulnerable versions. Otherwise, no immediate vulnerability-review trigger was identified for the primary product inventory in this window.
